notes: Implement (system-wide rule change, no bug.patch): soft-delete becomes a trash with a plan-bound restore window and a hard-delete purge that every counter, index and numbering rule must respect. Reference solution (11 files, ~295 changed lines) spans lib (RestoreRefusedError in soft-delete, mapped to conflict in errors.toAppError/isDomainError), types (issue.restored in TaskflowEventMap), schema + embedded migration (projects.issue_sequence high-water mark), issue repository (unpaged listArchivedIssuesBefore, purgeIssue deleting label links/comments/attachments in a transaction and recording the purged number, nextIssueNumber = max(max(number), sequence)+1), issue service (restoreIssue: tenant/NotFound/issue:archive with ownership escalation, then not_archived / expired / project_archived / quota refusals, emit issue.restored), usage/search/activity listeners for issue.restored, and the retention sweep (hard purge of every expired issue instead of the first page of 100 mixed rows, comment search docs, storage counter give-back). Hard because the rule touches four layers and collides with five existing rules: the ownership escalation (restore is an issue:archive action), the per-project quota (a restored issue counts), project archiving (cascaded issues cannot come back alone), the incremental usage counters (issues up on restore via a new event; storage down on purge so it matches a recount), and issue numbering (max(number) silently reuses a purged top number). The old sweep only looks at the first 100 issues by recency, which hides old trash behind newer issues. Hidden test: 10 cases (restore + event + counter + search + audit, permission incl. ownership, not_archived/project_archived refusals with toAppError, restore window by plan, quota, purge cascade + restore-after-purge + recently archived kept, storage give-back vs recount, >100 newer issues, number never reused, per-plan retention). Validation: pristine tsc 0 / 617 pass; pristine+hidden 10/10 fail; solution: patch -p1 clean, tsc 0, full suite 627 pass, hidden 3x 10/10 pass; naive A (restore with basic refusals + event, sweep deletes rows on its old first page) 7/10 fail; naive B (everything but quota, numbering and storage give-back) 3/10 fail.
